title: ICAN P9 Chinese Enduro Frame

takeaways.text: The full-carbon frame, including the swingarm, has 150 mm of rear travel and suits a 160–180 mm fork.
Despite a four-bar layout and a shock without lockout, he finds it climbs better than his Niner WFO.
A rear pivot bearing came loose on the first ride; after threadlock and retorquing the pivots it has been solid.
He paid about US$900 for the frame with custom paint; his build weighs about 31.6 lb, and he rides at about 225 lb.
For the 210×55 shock, 30×8 mm upper and 25.4×8 mm lower hardware fits better than the listed size, without the supplied spacers.
Cranks longer than 170 mm risk striking the frame; a Specialized Enduro chainstay protector fits, and the front triangle takes a full bottle.

disclosure: Owner video from 2020; whether the current P9 frame has changed since then is not established.
summary: An owner's notes on an ICAN P9 carbon enduro frame after his first rides.
